entries.abstract: A Lean 4 proof that for every nonnegative integer n, the distinct integers 1,...,n can be partitioned into nonempty sets of at most three elements, each having sum equal to a nonnegative integer power of three. This proves Conjecture 1 of Gurvich and Naumova, arXiv:2508.00946v3. The development constructs permutations with all prescribed nonzero displacements, derives signed zero-sum triple partitions, proves a contraction and complement-pair extension, and completes strong induction on n. All required finite certificates and unbounded sequence constructions are proved in Lean.
entries.title: gn-lean: the Gurvich–Naumova partition conjecture

entries.abstract: Proves the orthonormal double contraction of the actual corrected curvature derivative of a tangent connection on a smooth finite-dimensional real manifold. The Challenge exposes the corrected commutator and the smooth tangent-vector extensions explicitly; the Solution proves the identity for every supplied extension satisfying the stated hypotheses. The derivative symmetries and cyclic Bianchi equations are derived from torsion-freeness and metric compatibility, not assumed as abstract tensor data. No separate Einstein-divergence theorem is selected.

authors.name: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

entries.title: Double-contracted second Bianchi identity for metric-compatible torsion-free connections

entries.abstract: This project formalizes the global Kronecker–Weber theorem in Lean 4: every finite abelian extension of the rational numbers embeds into a cyclotomic field. For a number field L that is abelian Galois over the rationals, the selected declaration gives a positive integer n and a rational algebra embedding from L into CyclotomicField n ℚ. The proof is supplied by the ClassFieldTheory library at a fixed commit, using Lean 4.33.0 and Mathlib.
entries.title: The global Kronecker–Weber theorem in Lean 4

entries.abstract: GENERAL THEOREMS FIRST. Throughout, E is a finite-dimensional real inner product space of dimension n, Δ is Mathlib's coordinate-free Laplacian, HarmonicOnNhd its harmonic functions, and f : ℝ → ℝ is twice differentiable on (0, ∞) (two HasDerivAt hypotheses, with derivatives f', f''). (I) THE CLASSIFICATION OF RADIAL HARMONIC FUNCTIONS: (1) for n ≠ 2 and E ≠ 0, the radial function f ∘ ‖·‖ is harmonic on E ∖ {0} if and only if f(r) = a + b r^(2−n) on (0, ∞) for some real a, b; (2) for n = 2, if and only if f(r) = a + b log r — every radial harmonic function with a twice-differentiable profile is an affine function of the Newtonian potential, constants included, and of the logarithm in the plane. (II) THE LAPLACIAN OF RADIAL FUNCTIONS, away from the origin: (3) Δ(f ∘ ‖·‖)(x) = f''(‖x‖) + (n − 1) f'(‖x‖)/‖x‖, the radial Laplacian; (4) for g twice differentiable on (0, ∞), Δ(g(‖y‖²))(x) = 2n g'(‖x‖²) + 4‖x‖² g''(‖x‖²), the squared-norm parametrization; (5) for every real s, Δ(‖y‖^s)(x) = s (n + s − 2) ‖x‖^(s−2), the indicial identity (its consequence, not itself compared: for E ≠ 0, ‖y‖^s is harmonic away from 0 exactly when s (n + s − 2) = 0, at s = 0 and s = 2 − n, which coincide at n = 2); (6) Δ(log ‖y‖)(x) = (n − 2)/‖x‖²; (7) ‖y‖^(2−n) is harmonic on E ∖ {0} for every n — for n ≥ 3, up to its normalizing constant, the Newtonian kernel away from the origin (the normalization and the distributional identity −ΔΦ = δ at the origin, in Evans's sign convention, which make a normalized multiple of it the fundamental solution proper, are NOT formalized); at n = 2 the power is the constant 1 and the logarithmic case is (8); on the zero space the statement is vacuous; (8) log ‖y‖ is harmonic on E ∖ {0} when n = 2. (III) THE RADIAL EQUATION, the one-variable content of (1)-(2): (9) for n ≠ 2, f'' + (n − 1) f'/r = 0 on (0, ∞) if and only if f(r) = a + b r^(2−n) there for some a, b; (10) for n = 2, if and only if f(r) = a + b log r. (IV) THE STABILITY OF CIRCULAR ORBITS, general in the real exponent: for the effective potential U(r) = a/r² − b/r^p on (0, ∞), a, b > 0, p > 0 real — the radial potential of a body with angular momentum under a central attraction with force law 1/r^(p+1) — (11) U'(r) = 0 iff r^(2−p) = 2a/(bp), the circular-orbit condition (for p ≠ 2 that equation has exactly one positive solution, whence "the circular orbit" below — a consequence of (11), not itself compared; in the plane "the circular orbit r = √(2a/b)" names the point of (19)); (12) at a circular orbit U''(r) = 2a(2 − p)/r⁴; (13) for p < 2 the circular orbit r* = (2a/(bp))^(1/(2−p)) is a local minimum of U (Mathlib's non-strict IsLocalMin) — stable; (14) for p > 2 it is a local maximum — unstable; (15) for p > 2 U has no local minimum on (0, ∞) at all (Ehrenfest's reading, that bounded motion between two radii is then impossible, is not formalized); (16) U''(r*) r*⁴/(2a) = 2 − p, the square of the ratio of the radial to the angular frequency of small oscillations about the circular orbit, which the local step of Bertrand's argument requires to be the square of a rational number for a near-circular orbit to close. The boundary p = 2, where the two terms of U have the same power, is covered by the critical-point and second-derivative identities (11)-(12), whose only hypothesis on the exponent is p > 0, and is excluded from the stability conclusions (13)-(15) and the frequency identity (16), all of which require p ≠ 2; among the instances it is n = 4, where (17) with a ≠ b yields no local minimum (the potential (a − b)/r² has no critical point) while the sub-case a = b, where U vanishes, is excluded; the table's 'unstable' cell at n = 4 is not compared. THE INSTANCES (17)-(23), with p = n − 2 for the Newtonian potential in n ≥ 3 dimensions and the logarithmic potential in the plane: (17) for n ≥ 3 and a ≠ b a stable circular orbit exists iff n = 3 (a ≠ b excludes n = 4, a = b, where U vanishes identically and every point is a non-strict minimum); (18) for n ≥ 5 the effective potential has no local minimum on (0, ∞); (19) in the plane, for a/r² + b log r, the circular orbit r = √(2a/b) is stable; (20) the quantity of (16) is 4 − n for n ≥ 3, n ≠ 4, hence 1 at n = 3; (21) in the plane it equals 2; (22) in the plane its square root is irrational (it is √2 by (21); this statement asserts irrationality only); (23) ‖x‖^(2−n) is harmonic on ℝⁿ ∖ {0} for every n; for n ≥ 3, up to its normalizing constant, the Newtonian kernel away from the origin, with the same disclosure as (7). THE APPLICATION: Ehrenfest's argument of 1917 (KNAW Proceedings 20 (1918) 200-209, §1 and Appendix I) that the stability of planetary orbits singles out three spatial dimensions. He deduces the n-dimensional force law from the Laplace–Poisson equation (the Laplace half is statement (7), harmonicity away from the source; the Poisson half, the point source, is not formalized; the classification (1)-(2) makes "the radial harmonic function" a theorem), reduces the motion to the radial equation ṙ = (1/r)√(A r² + B r^(4−n) − C²), and tabulates three columns — circular trajectories; motions between two positive values of r; motion to the infinite — for n ≥ 4 (unstable, impossible, possible), n = 3 (stable, possible and moreover closed, possible), n = 2 (stable, possible and not closed, impossible). Statements (17)-(22) are the extrema and frequency identities of the effective potential behind the first two columns for n ≥ 5, n = 3, n = 2 — a local minimum where the table says stable, no local minimum where it says bounded motion is impossible, the frequency ratio where it says closed or not closed; the passage from those identities to trajectories (bounded motion, closure, the third column), the n = 4 cell, and Bertrand's global theorem (1873) are not formalized. Tangherlini (1963) extended the argument to the n-dimensional Schwarzschild field; Caruso and Xavier (1987) and Tegmark (1997) discuss its epistemological status and call it Ehrenfest's argument, as does this entry ("Ehrenfest's theorem" names his 1927 quantum-mechanical result). NOT formalized: Bertrand's theorem, the third column and the n = 4 cell of the table, the derivation of the effective potential from the equations of motion, the relativistic extension, the wave-equation half of Ehrenfest's paper (Huygens' principle in odd dimensions), and any statement about the actual dimension of physical space — the theorems classify radial functions and a family of effective potentials; the reading that the stable case is the world we observe is Ehrenfest's, cited, not compared. PRIOR ART, as of the 2026-09-02 sweep: Mathlib has the Laplacian on inner product spaces (InnerProductSpace.laplacian, laplacian_eq_iteratedFDeriv_orthonormalBasis), harmonic functions (HarmonicAt, HarmonicOnNhd, harmonicAt_congr_nhds) with complex-analytic examples — in particular AnalyticAt.harmonicAt_log_norm, which gives log |z| harmonic on ℂ ∖ {0}, the n = 2 case of (8) in the complex model obtained through complex analysis — the second- derivative test (isLocalMin_of_deriv_deriv_pos), the mean-value lemmas IsOpen.exists_is_const_of_deriv_eq_zero and IsOpen.exists_eq_add_of_deriv_eq, and real powers; it has no Laplacian of a radial function, no harmonic power of the norm, no classification of radial harmonic functions, no central-force mechanics, and no formalization of Ehrenfest's argument. No formalization of the classification of radial harmonic functions, of Ehrenfest's argument, of the harmonic Newtonian potential in general dimension, or of Bertrand's theorem was found in the surveyed prover ecosystems (Mathlib and its archive, the Isabelle AFP, the Coq Mathematical Components and Coquelicot analysis libraries). The proof module descends from the author's public pdt-lean development (pinned below), where none of these statements was ever a compared statement. Axioms on every compared theorem: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, audited in-build.
entries.title: Radial harmonic functions on a real inner product space: the classification, the Laplacian of radial functions, and the stability of circular orbits for power-law central forces; Ehrenfest's dimensionality argument (1917) as the application

entries.abstract: Lean formalization of the paper's finite skew-symmetric path instance, exact prefix-deletion completion oracle, deterministic oracle-pruned DFS, correctness and duplicate-freedom, and an executable DFS event trace whose extracted first-output, inter-output, post-output, and no-output work intervals satisfy the paper-level depth/LCP bounds.

entries.abstract: Construction of the massive Gaussian Free Field in Euclidean spacetime of any dimension d >= 2 as a probability measure on the tempered distributions S'(R^d), and a proof that it satisfies all of the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms: OS0 analyticity, OS1 regularity, OS2 Euclidean invariance, OS3 reflection positivity, and OS4 clustering and ergodicity. The OS axioms are the conditions under which a Euclidean field theory reconstructs a relativistic quantum field theory obeying the Wightman axioms, so the free field is the base case of constructive quantum field theory on which interacting constructions are built. The development is dimension-generic: one proof parameterized by d, consuming the free covariance only through a typeclass whose per-dimension input is a single closed-form radial kernel identified with the proper-time integral, with concrete instances at d = 2, 3, 4, 5. The result addresses three research audiences. In constructive quantum field theory, the free field satisfying OS0-OS4 is the base case (Glimm-Jaffe, ch. 6) on which interacting constructions such as P(phi)_2 and phi^4_3 are built, so a machine-checked base case is the reusable starting point for any formalized interacting construction. The analytic chain is proved rather than assumed: the Minlos theorem and the Hilbert-nuclearity of Schwartz space are consumed from the bochner and gaussian-field developments as theorems, nuclearity in the general form for Schwartz functions on any finite-dimensional real normed space, so every headline result depends on nothing beyond Lean's three foundational axioms. In stochastic quantization and singular SPDEs, the massive GFF constructed here is the reference Gaussian and the invariant measure of the free dynamics in every dimension treated. And for researchers formalizing quantum field theory in various dimensions, this is, to our knowledge, the first machine-checked verification of the Osterwalder-Schrader axioms — the literature search supporting that statement (scope, terms, dates, and the related-but-distinct work found) is documented in docs/novelty.md of this repository — with the dimension-generic propagator typeclass as the designed extension point for further covariances and dimensions.
entries.title: mrdouglasny/OSforGFF-comparator

entries.abstract: Twenty-one theorems and thirty-three definitions, machine-checked in Lean 4 against Mathlib v4.32.0: the Schwarzschild, Schwarzschild-de Sitter (Kottler), Reissner-Nordstrom (with the Maxwell stress tensor defined and G = 8 pi T proved in all sixteen components), ingoing Vaidya (null dust of rank at most one, rank one wherever dm/dv ≠ 0, for a merely once-differentiable mass function), spatially flat FLRW (both Friedmann equations in Einstein-tensor form), static de Sitter, Minkowski-in-spherical and Kiselev metrics, together with Birkhoff uniqueness in the areal static gauge and the n != 2 equivalence of the two forms of the vacuum equations. The results are classical and NO NEW MATHEMATICS IS CLAIMED: this is a proof of concept for the definitions. Lean checks that a proof establishes a statement, not that a definition means what its name says, so the entry certifies its sign, index and contraction conventions by computing textbook solutions with them -- including four NONZERO answers (de Sitter R = 12/L^2, Reissner-Nordstrom R_thetatheta = Q^2/r^2, Vaidya R_vv = 2 (dm/dv)/r^2, Kiselev R_thetatheta = -3wc r^-(3w+1)), because a curvature definition that was accidentally identically zero would still prove every vacuum theorem here. Scope: everything is a computation in ONE FIXED CHART, an open subset of R^4 -- no atlas, no manifold, no coordinate-independence theorem, no maximal extension, and horizons and coordinate poles lie outside every statement. NOT compared: Ricci symmetry R_bd = R_db in general (it needs Clairaut for the coordinate partial derivative, which Mathlib supplies only for fderiv) or the Bianchi identities; Maxwell's own equations; any matter model, fluid or energy condition beyond the single defined Maxwell stress tensor; non-flat FLRW; the outgoing Vaidya chart. Audience: general relativists, for whom this is the definitional layer a junction-condition or thin-shell statement would be written against, and the formalization community, for whom it is coverage-creating rather than coverage-duplicating. Mathlib v4.32.0 contains no curvature of any kind -- christoffel, ricci, scalarCurvature, Lorentzian, PseudoRiemannian and five further names return zero hits across all 8,264 .lean files at the pinned revision, and its one metric structure hard-codes positive definiteness -- so the entire chain is defined inline in the Challenge.
